items.title: All Blacks beat Wallabies 43-21 in Sydney to sweep Bledisloe Cup series
items.why: New Zealand beat Australia 43-21 at Stadium Australia in Sydney on Saturday, a week after a 50-19 win in Auckland, to take the two-Test series 2-0. It was Australia's 13th straight defeat by the All Blacks, who have held the Bledisloe Cup since 2003.

items.title: Two tankers attacked off Saudi Arabia's Gulf coast as ship attacks surge
items.why: Two tankers were hit on Friday about 70 nautical miles off Jubail, Saudi Arabia, one by a rocket-propelled grenade from a small boat, Britain's UKMTO agency says. All crew were reported safe. UKMTO says October is the busiest month yet for reported attacks near the Strait of Hormuz.
items.matters: Before the war about a fifth of the world's oil exports passed through Hormuz, so attacks there push up fuel prices.

items.title: Canada end England's long unbeaten run in women's rugby with 24-21 win
items.why: Canada beat world champions England 24-21 in Toronto on Friday, England's first defeat since the 2022 World Cup final. Shoshanah Seumanutafa scored the winning try with three minutes left, in front of 18,621 fans, a North American record for a stand-alone women's match.
items.matters: It was Canada's first win over England since 2016; the two sides meet again in Ottawa next Friday.

items.title: Amazon deforestation in Brazil falls to lowest level since records began
items.why: Brazil's Amazon lost about 3,335 sq km of forest in the 12 months to July 2026, roughly 42% less than a year earlier and the lowest since satellite records began in 1988, the space agency Inpe said on 16 October. Clearing in the Cerrado savanna also hit a record low.
items.matters: The figures are provisional and come days before Brazil's 25 October presidential run-off between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro.

items.title: Tech shares slide and oil nears $110; Nasdaq's worst week since June
items.why: US technology shares fell on Friday 16 October. The Nasdaq dropped 2.1% on the day and 4.5% over the week as investors questioned the debt-funded AI building boom. Brent crude touched $110 a barrel, its highest since May, after attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
items.matters: Dearer oil pushes up inflation and keeps borrowing costs high; the 10-year US Treasury yield is around 5.1%.

items.title: US measles cases reach 4,410 this year as Pennsylvania outbreak grows
items.why: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 4,410 measles cases in 2026 as of 15 October, up 330 in a week, with 451 people treated in hospital. Pennsylvania, the largest outbreak, reports more than 1,200 cases and at least five deaths, state officials say.
items.matters: About 96% of cases were in people who were unvaccinated or whose vaccination status was unknown, the CDC says.

items.title: South African rugby player Hyron Andrews dies in France before match
items.why: Hyron Andrews, a 31-year-old lock for Johannesburg's Lions, died on Friday at the team hotel on Île de Ré, near La Rochelle in western France, the day before their Champions Cup game. The local prosecutor has opened an investigation and ordered a post-mortem.
items.matters: The Lions will play the match in his honour, with a moment's silence at all European club games this weekend.

items.title: Delhi police detain youth protest leader before rally against India's election chief
items.why: Police in India's capital, New Delhi, detained the founder of the youth-led 'Cockroach' movement on Friday before a rally demanding election chief Gyanesh Kumar's resignation; media reports say he was later arrested. Protesters object to a voter-roll review that removed more than 130 million names.
items.matters: Who can vote in the world's largest democracy is at stake; the commission denies bias and says wrongly removed voters can re-enrol.

items.title: Ethiopia names a six-month interim government for Tigray
items.why: Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on Friday named a federal caretaker administration to run the northern Tigray region for six months, promising elections afterwards. It follows an offensive by the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) in September; Reuters reports federal forces have since taken the regional capital, Mekelle.
items.matters: Tigray was the scene of a 2020–22 war. The TPLF, which once ran the region, had not yet responded.

items.title: Bangladesh dengue deaths reach 335 this year as cases pass 108,000
items.why: Bangladesh's health directorate reported four more dengue deaths on 16 October, bringing this year's toll to 335, with 108,440 cases recorded. September was the deadliest month so far, with 148 deaths, and infections are continuing past the usual June-to-September season.
items.matters: Dengue, spread by mosquitoes, has no specific treatment; Bangladesh's government has ordered neighbourhood awareness campaigns to curb it.

items.changed: Updated: Trudy has weakened to about 150 km/h winds; a hurricane warning now covers Manzanillo to Cabo Corrientes.
items.title: Hurricane Trudy nears Mexico's Pacific coast after weakening
items.why: Trudy had winds near 150 km/h early on Saturday, down from major-storm strength on Friday, the US National Hurricane Center said. Its centre should pass very close to Colima and Jalisco on Saturday night and Sunday. A hurricane warning runs from Manzanillo to Cabo Corrientes.
items.matters: Forecasters warn of heavy rain that could cause life-threatening flooding and mudslides in Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco.

items.changed: Updated: Champi has become a Category 4 typhoon; Guam is at its highest readiness level and coastal areas are being evacuated.
items.title: Typhoon Champi strengthens to Category 4 as it nears Guam
items.why: Champi became a Category 4 typhoon on Saturday, the Joint Typhoon Warning Center said, and should pass just south of Guam early on Sunday with winds near 240 km/h. Guam is at its highest readiness level, and people in coastal and flood-prone areas were told to evacuate.
items.matters: Forecasters warn that most metal-roofed homes could be badly damaged and power cuts could last days to weeks.

items.title: Brazil's electoral court orders Meta to treat Lula and Bolsonaro equally
items.why: A judge at Brazil's top electoral court ordered Meta on 15 October to give President Lula and challenger Flávio Bolsonaro equal reach before the 25 October run-off, or pay 500,000 reais (about $98,000) a day. Most of the court backed it on 16 October. Meta denies bias.
items.matters: It tests how far courts can police social media algorithms during an election.

items.title: Indonesian shares fall 11% after MSCI proposes downgrading the market
items.why: Jakarta's main share index fell about 11% on 16 October, its steepest one-day drop since 1998. The index provider MSCI had proposed moving Indonesia from 'emerging' to 'standalone' market status, citing opaque shareholdings and suspected coordinated trading. The rupiah neared a record low.
items.matters: Funds that track MSCI's emerging-market indexes could be forced to sell Indonesian shares.

items.title: Milwaukee Brewers sweep Dodgers to reach first World Series since 1982
items.why: The Milwaukee Brewers came from 4-0 down to beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 in Los Angeles on Thursday night, winning the National League Championship Series 4-0. The two-time defending champions are out; the World Series starts in Milwaukee on 23 October.
items.matters: Milwaukee, Major League Baseball's smallest media market, is chasing the first championship in the club's history.

items.title: Tesla shows a Roadster sports car that hops into the air
items.why: At a SpaceX site in Texas on 15 October, Elon Musk unveiled a new Tesla Roadster that used compressed-air thrusters to hop over other cars and land. Production is due in 2028, and the flying version is not approved for public roads.
items.matters: The US aviation regulator says it is not an aircraft, so it is unclear who would regulate it.

items.title: Hasun, South Korea's oldest hippopotamus, dies aged 46
items.why: Seoul Grand Park, just south of the South Korean capital, said Hasun died peacefully with no sign of illness, apparently of old age. Born in 1980, she was among the first animals at the park's zoo when it opened in 1984.
items.matters: Hippos usually live 40 to 50 years, so Hasun reached the upper end of that range.

items.changed: Updated: two missiles hit Aden airport on Friday night; no casualties reported.
items.title: Houthi missiles hit Aden airport a day after deadly palace attack
items.why: Two missiles struck the airport in Aden, seat of Yemen's government, on Friday night, landing about 500 metres from a plane preparing to take off, officials say; no one was hurt. Thursday's Houthi strike on the presidential palace killed at least five, the health ministry says.
items.matters: The Houthis say they are targeting Saudi forces in Aden, widening their fight with Saudi Arabia and Yemen's government.

items.title: Police clash with marchers in Buenos Aires over university funding
items.why: On Thursday, thousands of students and lecturers marched on Argentina's Congress in Buenos Aires, demanding President Javier Milei's government apply a university funding law. Police used tear gas and water cannon after some protesters threw stones. La Nación reports more than 30 people detained.
items.matters: The government says the law lacks funding; a University of Buenos Aires study says real funding fell about 40% since 2023.

items.title: U2 announce world stadium tour opening in Latin America in 2027
items.why: The Irish band will open 'The Greatest Show on Earth' tour in Mexico City on 23 February 2027, then play São Paulo and Buenos Aires, with Beck as support. Their 16th album, Carnaval De Luz, their first in nine years, comes out on 13 November.
items.matters: It is U2's first stadium tour since 2019; dates for Europe and North America are due in the coming weeks.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launch trailer reveals Justice as the game's composers
items.why: Rockstar Games released the launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto VI on 15 October and named French electronic duo Justice as composers of its score. The trailer features their new song with Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard; the game arrives on 19 November.
items.matters: The game's 34-track soundtrack album, out the same day, also features Travis Scott, Cardi B and Rauw Alejandro.

items.title: Swedish parliament rejects Magdalena Andersson as prime minister
items.why: On Thursday, Sweden's parliament voted 248 to 99 against Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson becoming prime minister, a month after the 13 September election. Only her own party backed her, as the Left and Centre parties remain split over who should join a government.
items.matters: Parliament gets four attempts to approve a prime minister. If all four fail, Sweden must hold a snap election.

items.title: Jon Rahm agrees to leave LIV Golf, giving up remaining payments
items.why: Spanish golfer Jon Rahm has reached a separation agreement with LIV Golf, filed on 14 October in the league's bankruptcy case in New Jersey, USA. He drops all money claims, reportedly over $100 million, and his team stake; a judge must approve it on 5 November.
items.matters: LIV, in bankruptcy since September, loses one of its biggest names as it tries to relaunch in 2027.

items.title: World timekeepers vote to scrap the leap second from 2027
items.why: Delegates at the General Conference on Weights and Measures in Versailles, France, voted by majority on 15 October to stop adding leap seconds from 20 May 2027. Official time will instead be allowed to drift up to an hour from Earth's rotation.
items.matters: Leap seconds, 27 added since 1972, can disrupt computer systems; a 'leap hour' is not expected to be needed for centuries.

items.title: Amsterdam zoo hornbill gets world's first pair of 3D-printed beak prostheses
items.why: A male southern ground hornbill at Artis zoo in Amsterdam broke both halves of his beak while digging for food. Specialists from Utrecht University and UMC Utrecht rebuilt them with 3D-printed parts fixed on with titanium, and within two days he was catching mice again.
items.matters: The zoo says it is the first known bird to have both upper and lower beak restored this way.

items.title: Iranian director Majid Majidi's 'Midday Meal' wins top prize at Busan festival
items.why: The film, about a rural schoolteacher, won the Busan Award for best film on Thursday as South Korea's 31st Busan International Film Festival closed. A jury led by Chinese director Zhang Yimou chose it unanimously from 13 Asian films.
items.matters: Under new rules, the win lets the film go straight into the Oscars' international feature race.

items.title: Australia edge New Zealand 24-22 in Rugby League World Cup opener
items.why: Australia beat New Zealand 24-22 at Sydney's Allianz Stadium on 15 October in the opening match of the Rugby League World Cup. Debutant Jack Bostock scored three tries, including the late winner, before a crowd of 41,255.

items.title: IMF raises sub-Saharan Africa growth forecast but warns of rising inflation
items.why: The International Monetary Fund now expects sub-Saharan Africa's economies to grow 4.5% in 2026, up from the 4.3% it forecast in April, it said on 15 October. It expects median inflation to rise to 4.3% this year and 5% in 2027, while aid to Africa falls a further 12%.
items.matters: The IMF says the region has little room to absorb another shock, such as renewed energy disruption or a strong El Niño.

items.changed: Updated: leaders adopted the Yerevan Declaration on 16 October, and new figures show nature funding falling short before COP17.
items.title: Leaders adopt Yerevan nature declaration as funding falls short before COP17
items.why: Leaders meeting in Armenia's capital, Yerevan, on 16 October adopted a declaration calling for faster action and more money to halt nature loss by 2030. A UN review this week found fewer than half of national nature targets are on track. COP17 talks open on 19 October.
items.matters: Countries raised $75–92 billion a year for nature in 2023–25, under half the $200 billion goal, OECD data show.

items.changed: Updated: a fourth body was found on Friday; three people are still missing and more rain is forecast.
items.title: Three still missing after Istanbul's worst floods in over 80 years
items.why: At least four people have died in floods in Turkey's largest city, Istanbul, officials say, after a man's body was found in Sarıyer district on Friday. Rescuers are still searching for three people, and forecasters warned of more heavy rain on Saturday.
items.matters: Turkey's environment minister links the floods to climate change and building near rivers. He chairs the upcoming COP31 climate talks.

items.title: H5N1 bird flu found on Australia's sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island
items.why: Australia has confirmed H5N1 bird flu in an elephant seal and a kelp gull on Macquarie Island, a World Heritage site about 1,500 km south-east of Tasmania, the island's first case. Officials say the risk to humans is low; experts expect many seals to die this breeding season.
items.matters: The island is a key breeding ground for southern elephant seals, which are highly vulnerable to the virus.

items.changed: Updated: service partly restored; Trump denies ordering the limits.
items.title: Ukraine says Starlink partly restored; Trump denies ordering the drone limits
items.why: Ukraine says Starshield, SpaceX's military version of Starlink, is working again but still cuts out above 160 km/h, which hampers its drones. Elon Musk says the US government sets the limits. On 16 October President Trump said he did not order them and did not think Musk did.
items.matters: It shows how much a war can depend on one private company's satellites.

items.changed: Updated: Kenya confirmed a third case on 16 October; Congo has passed 9,200 confirmed cases.
items.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case, another relative of the first patient
items.why: Kenya's health ministry said on Friday 16 October that a 65-year-old woman, already in quarantine as a close relative of the first two patients, has tested positive. It says 127 of 130 contacts are in quarantine and there is no sign of wider spread.
items.matters: Congo's outbreak, linked to Kenya's cases, has passed 9,270 confirmed cases and 4,470 deaths, US CDC figures show.
